# Upgrade guide — Exeris Kernel 0.5.x → 0.10.x

**Status:** Tracked / consumer-facing
**Applies to:** `eu.exeris.kernel:exeris-kernel-spi` and the Community drivers built on it
**Evidence:** [`spi-api-history.md`](./spi-api-history.md) — every claim below is generated by
`tools/spi-api-diff/spi-api-diff.sh`, not written by hand

---

## Who needs this

You are on 0.5.x and want to move to 0.10.x in one hop. This guide lists **every**
binary-incompatible change to the public SPI across that range, and what to write instead.

It is deliberately short, because the range is mostly additive: of the nine releases between
0.5.0 and 0.10.2, **three** carry a binary-incompatible change to the public SPI and six are
purely additive. The full per-release evidence is in [`spi-api-history.md`](./spi-api-history.md).

Two things this guide does **not** cover: Community driver internals (`eu.exeris.kernel.community.*`
is not a consumer contract — see [`../stability-matrix.md`](../stability-matrix.md)), and behavioural
change that is source-compatible. For the latter, read the per-release notes under `docs/release/`.

---

## The short version

| If you use… | You must change something |
|---|---|
| `PersistenceEngine.capabilities()` / `PersistenceProvider.dialect()` / `DatabaseDialect` | yes — §1 |
| `TransportEngine.capabilities()` | yes — §1 |
| `TelemetryConfig` (as a record: canonical constructor or the off-heap accessor) | yes — §2 |
| `EventStreamAppender` / `new EventTypeSpec(...)` | yes — §3 |
| anything else in `eu.exeris.kernel.spi.*` | no |

If none of the rows above appear in your code, upgrading 0.5.x → 0.10.2 is a version bump.

---

## 1. 0.5.0 → 0.6.0 — capability descriptors removed

The largest single change in the range. Three types were removed outright:

- `eu.exeris.kernel.spi.persistence.DatabaseDialect` (and its nested `ImmutableDatabaseDialect`)
- `eu.exeris.kernel.spi.persistence.PersistenceEngineCapabilities`
- `eu.exeris.kernel.spi.transport.TransportEngineCapabilities`

…taking three members with them:

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `PersistenceEngine.capabilities()` | No direct replacement. The descriptor was split: use `healthCheckDetailed()` for liveness and `stats()` for counters. |
| `PersistenceProvider.dialect(PersistenceConfig)` | No replacement — dialect selection became a driver-internal concern. |
| `TransportEngine.capabilities()` | Discrete accessors on the same interface: `mode()` (returns `TransportMode`), `engineName()`, `stats()`. |

**Why it happened.** `DatabaseDialect` enumerated concrete engines (`POSTGRESQL`, `MYSQL`, `SQLITE`)
and parsed JDBC URLs *inside the SPI*. That is an implementation detail of a driver sitting in the
contract module — a direct breach of The Wall ([ADR-006](../adr/ADR-006.link.md)).
The capability records were removed in the same pass because a frozen descriptor cannot describe a
provider set that is discovered at runtime; discrete accessors can.

**Porting sketch.** Code that branched on a dialect moves the branch behind its own abstraction or
into the driver; code that read `capabilities()` for a boolean reads the specific accessor instead.
If you were using `DatabaseDialect.fromUrl(...)` for your own routing, that method is gone — keep a
copy in your application, it has no kernel dependency.

---

## 2. 0.8.1 → 0.9.0 — `TelemetryConfig` off-heap component renamed

One removal, and it is a rename:

```java
// 0.5.0 – 0.8.1
public record TelemetryConfig(boolean consoleSinkEnabled, boolean jfrSinkEnabled,
                              String fileSinkPath, long blackBoxOffHeapBytes, int maxEventQueueDepth)

// 0.9.0 onward
public record TelemetryConfig(boolean consoleSinkEnabled, boolean jfrSinkEnabled,
                              String fileSinkPath, long glassBoxOffHeapBytes, int maxEventQueueDepth)
```

`blackBoxOffHeapBytes()` → `glassBoxOffHeapBytes()`. Semantics, validation, and position in the
canonical constructor are unchanged; only the name moved, aligning the carrier with the *Glass-Box*
terminology used everywhere else (see [`../glossary.md`](../glossary.md)).

Positional construction (`new TelemetryConfig(a, b, c, d, e)`) is unaffected. You only touch code
that called the accessor by name or used a record deconstruction pattern naming the component.

---

## 3. 0.9.0 → 0.10.0 — events log-ordering (`preview` surface)

`eu.exeris.kernel.spi.events` is labelled **`preview`** in the stability matrix, so these changes are
permitted by the declared policy rather than an exception to it. They still break source, so they are
listed here.

**`EventStreamAppender.append`** — the three-argument form is gone; append now carries an expected
version and returns a result, which is what makes optimistic concurrency expressible
([ADR-049](../adr/ADR-049-events-log-ordering-and-optimistic-concurrency-boundary.md)):

```java
// 0.10.0-
void append(StreamId streamId, EventDescriptor descriptor, EventPayload payload);
// 0.10.0+
AppendResult append(StreamId streamId, long expectedVersion, /* … */);
```

Pass the version you read the stream at. If you are appending without a concurrency check, pass the
current version you just observed — there is no "don't care" sentinel by design, because a blind
append is exactly what the ADR set out to make impossible.

**`EventTypeSpec`** — the canonical constructor gained a `topic` component
([ADR-050](../adr/ADR-050-events-binding-agnostic-topic.md)), so
`new EventTypeSpec(name, ordinal, persistent, ordered)` no longer resolves.

The static factories were kept and are the recommended entry point — **if you used
`EventTypeSpec.of(...)` or `ofPersistent(...)`, nothing changes.** Only direct constructor calls
break. Three- and four-argument overloads taking an explicit `topic` were added alongside.

---

## Releases that need nothing

`0.6.0 → 0.7.0`, `0.7.0 → 0.7.1`, `0.7.1 → 0.8.0`, `0.8.0 → 0.8.1`, `0.10.0 → 0.10.1`,
`0.10.1 → 0.10.2` add SPI surface without removing or reshaping any of it. No action.

One note for the record: `0.8.0 → 0.8.1` is a *patch* release that carried an API **addition**
(japicmp classifies it as a minor-level change). It breaks nothing, but it is a semver
irregularity, and it is the kind of thing the gate described below now surfaces at release time
rather than months later.

---

## How this document is kept honest

The tables above are not maintained by hand. `tools/spi-api-diff/spi-api-diff.sh` compiles the SPI
module at each revision straight from git — the module depends only on `java.*` / `jdk.*`, so every
revision in history builds with nothing but a JDK — and diffs the results with japicmp, classifying
each finding by the maturity label declared in [`../stability-matrix.md`](../stability-matrix.md).

The same script runs as a CI gate on every build: a binary-incompatible change to a surface declared
`stable` fails the build. See [`spi-api-history.md`](./spi-api-history.md) for the generated record
and `tools/spi-api-diff/README.md` for how to run it yourself.
